name: Peak near Shackleton
source: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.19863v1 Table 3 (ID 1223, region Site07 'Peak Near Shackleton', TOPSIS rank 15 of 20)
note: Artemis III candidate-region point from a GIS ranking, about 1 deg (30 km) from the pole; NOT on Shackleton crater rim. 5 m LOLA DEMs. Paper reports no sunlit % for it.

name: Shackleton rim
source: Glaser et al. 2018, NTRS 20170007365, Table 1 row Shackleton S 'This study' (surface level, 20 m/px LOLA DTM, 2017-2037)
note: Most-illuminated spot on the Shackleton crater rim: 81.0 % average sunlit, 85.5 % Sun visible, longest shadow 221 h. Mazarico 2011 (240 m/px): -89.78, 204.27 E, 86.7 %.

name: Connecting Ridge
source: Glaser et al. 2018, NTRS 20170007365, Table 1 row Connecting Ridge C1 'This study' (surface level)
note: 76.0 % average sunlit, 81.3 % Sun visible, longest shadow 268 h (Mazarico 2011: 89.0 %, 141.12 h). Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache.

name: Nobile Rim 2
source: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.19863v1 Table 3 (ID 358, region DM2 'Nobile Rim 2', TOPSIS rank 1)
note: Top-ranked point in that paper's equal-weight ranking; no sunlit % reported.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
source: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.19863v1 Table 3 (ID 726, region SL2 'de Gerlache Rim 2', rank 18; longitude printed 61 10 2.35 'O' = west)

name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
note: Athena's actual resting place: inside a 20 m crater, lying on its side after landing 6 Mar 2025. LROC gives no uncertainty. Intended site was -84.78, 29.13 (images/1401).

name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
note: Landed 22 Feb 2024 on a slope near Malapert A, about 1.5 km from the target (Intuitive Machines). NASA gives no uncertainty or datum.
